title: Investigation of maintaining factors of depressive disorders in patients with psoriasis
summary:
Many people in Germany suffer from a skin disease called psoriasis. The main symptom is a persistent inflammation of the skin that leads to major restrictions in the quality of life of those affected. Many people with psoriasis also suffer from depression. Psoriasis and depression influence each other, although the exact mechanisms are not yet fully understood.
In recent years, better drugs have come onto the market to treat moderate and severe cases of psoriasis. However, not all patients experience an improvement in mood during the course of treatment as well. We would like to investigate the role of changes in body image over the course of therapy for the improvement of mood.
For this reason, we will record the mood and, in particular, symptoms of depression as well as changes in the patients' body image over the course of the first 28 weeks of treatment. This study could provide important information as to whether certain patients require psychotherapeutic treatment in addition to psoriasis treatment.

interventions.name: Patients with plaque psoriasis who initiate systemic therapy will complete various questionnaires before the start and after 16 and 28 weeks of therapy. In addition, a psychological diagnostic interview will be conducted at the beginning and after 28 weeks.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients suffering from plaque psoriasis with an indication for systemic treatment
Exclusion criteria:
• Pregnant or breast-feeding women or lack of willingness to use effective contraception
• Insufficient communication skills in the German language, dementia or functional analphabetism
• Lack of capacity or will to consent to the study
• Existing contraindication to anti-psoriatic systemic treatment
